mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate indicates an easing of monetary policy, which may lead to increased borrowing and investment, thus driving up S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns despite falling FEDFUNDS, the hypothesis is invalidated.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the unemployment rate suggests economic weakness, potentially leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE increases by 0.2pp in one month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 rises despite UNRATE increases, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent increases in unemployment and decreases in payroll employment signal economic contraction, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: Positive S&P 500 returns despite concurrent labor market weakness invalidate this.

mechanism_narrative: Rising consumer prices may lead to tighter monetary policy, negatively impacting S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL increases by 0.5% in one month
failure_condition: If S&P 500 rises despite CPI increases, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing housing starts indicate strong demand, which may boost S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: Negative S&P 500 returns despite rising HOUST invalidate this.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production may signal supply chain issues, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decreases by 0.5% in one month
failure_condition: If S&P 500 rises despite INDPRO drops, the hypothesis is invalid.

mechanism_narrative: High federal funds rates combined with rising unemployment may indicate stagflation, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: Positive S&P 500 returns despite high FEDFUNDS and rising UNRATE invalidate this.

mechanism_narrative: GDP growth in an early-cycle expansion may boost consumer and business confidence, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 increases by 0.2% in one quarter
failure_condition: Negative S&P 500 returns despite GDP growth invalidate this hypothesis.
